meta.scope_clause_template: representative of this row; not asserted true of all {N} chips carrying this protocol_id.
meta.datasheets_not_committed: No datasheets/ tree resolves on this branch (F-140-08); doc/PROTOCOLS.md already cites paths under such a tree that do not exist here. Citations in this sidecar are therefore self-describing: vendor, part, document number/title, revision or date, and section/figure -- never a repository path. Where the v1.16 archive still holds the original PDF, it can be recovered with: `git -C firestarter show v1.16-protocol-first-architecture-rebuild:datasheets/<slug>/<file>.pdf > <file>.pdf`. The TI TMS 2516 PDF recovered this way has no text layer (Acrobat 5.0 Scan Plug-in, zero embedded fonts) and must be rendered before it can be read, for example with `pdftoppm -png -r 170 <file>.pdf page`.
meta.why_two_checks: A citation that can drift from its value is not a citation. The gate compares each cell's recorded value against the live table (test_recorded_values_match_the_live_table) in addition to checking that the (row, column) coverage is an exact bijection (test_citations_cover_every_cell_exactly_once) -- so a value that moves without its citation following is caught by the same mechanism that catches a cell shipping with no citation at all.
meta.how_to_update: If a value in include/eprom_params.h or src/proms/eprom_params.cpp legitimately changes, its citation in this file changes in the same commit, and the commit message states which cell changed, the new value, and the new basis. Never edit a value recorded here merely to make a surprise in the live table disappear -- that would defeat the entire point of the drift check.
meta.evidence_ceiling: verify_mode encodes WHEN to verify and never at what VCC. Every datasheet read for this table specifies its final verification pass at a raised VCC for threshold margin (ST M27C512/M27C1001: 1st VCC=6V, 2nd VCC=4.2V; Microchip 27C512A: VCC=VPP=4.5V/5.5V for the Express final check; AMD Am27C020: VCC=VPP=5.25V after programming at 6.25V). The RURP shield has no VCC-raise path -- the ~6.25V program-VCC ceiling this milestone measured is the practical ceiling for this hardware -- so a verify-VCC column could only ever record a value the firmware has no way to act on. D-02 forbids that column outright; this paragraph is the place that constraint is recorded in the same file as the numbers, not only in Phase 146's ledger.

named_divergences.statement: PROJECT.md's throughput table implies 3 for 0x07, but the shipped value is 0; the 22 Intel-family 1ms parts on this row (Intel 2764 / 2764A / 27128 / 27128A / 27512, TI TMS2764, NEC UPD2764, ST M2764A and the rest of the 1000 microsecond sub-population) genuinely want a 3xN margin pulse, which the 0x07 datasheets cited for the shipped value of 0 do not apply.
named_divergences.phase_146_handoff: Serving the Intel-family 1ms sub-population correctly requires splitting 0x07 into a second row, which TABLE-05's no-second-dispatch-key constraint forbids in this milestone. Recorded as a Phase 146 follow-up candidate, not silently dropped.

named_divergences.statement: PROJECT.md's own throughput table gives 0x08 a 3 x N x pulse overpulse, contradicting PROJECT.md's own prose ('not for Quick-Pulse / Flashrite / PRESTO, so it is gated per row') -- the two halves of the same document disagree with each other.
named_divergences.phase_146_handoff: D-06 resolves this in favour of the prose and the primary datasheets (three independent vendors specify no overprogram pulse): 0x08 overprogram_factor = 0 ships. Phase 146 / CLOSE-04 reconciles PROJECT.md's throughput table text against this finding.

named_divergences.statement: The justification sentence published on gh#15 and carried in PROJECT.md -- that 50ms 'is exactly the classic 2716 total programming time', derived as 100 x 500us -- is factually wrong. The TI TMS 2516 datasheet states its own total programming time for all bits is 100 seconds; 50ms is the per-location pulse width (t_w(PR) TYP), not a total.
named_divergences.phase_146_handoff: The value (50000us) is correct and has a genuine primary datasheet basis; only the published REASON is wrong. This phase records the correction without editing the posted gh#15 text or PROJECT.md; Phase 146 / CLOSE-04 reconciles the posted text.

cells.section: AC 'recommended timing requirements for programming' (p.141), parameter t_w(PR)
cells.quote: TI TMS 2516 AC table, verbatim: 't_w(PR) Pulse width, program pulse = MIN 45 / TYP 50 / MAX 55 ms.' Also p.138, verbatim: 'a 50-millisecond TTL high-level pulse should be applied to the PGM pin at each address location to be programmed. Maximum pulse width is 55 milliseconds.'
cells.scope: representative of this row; not asserted true of all 32 chips carrying this protocol_id.
cells.notes: CORRECTION THAT MUST BE RECORDED, NOT APPLIED HERE (F-140-07, see meta.named_divergences): the justification published on gh#15 and carried in PROJECT.md -- that 50ms 'is exactly the classic 2716 total programming time', derived as 100 x 500us -- is factually wrong. This same TI TMS 2516 datasheet states on its front page, verbatim: 'requiring a single 50-ms pulse... Total programming time for all bits is 100 seconds.' 50ms is the per-location pulse width, not the total. The VALUE (50000us = 50ms) has a genuine primary basis (t_w(PR) TYP = 50ms); the REASON published for it on gh#15 does not. Phase 146 / CLOSE-04 reconciles the posted text; this phase records the correction without editing the published comment.

cells.reasoned_from: no datasheet basis — reasoned from a termination bound. F-140-06: the floor is 250 -- reaching the 50ms energy cap needs 250 pulses at 200us (5 of 32 chips), 100 at 500us (21 chips), and 50 at 1000us (6 chips), so a backstop below 250 pre-empts the energy cap on the 200us sub-population and silently under-programs 5 chips. 255 is the smallest uint8_t-representable value clearing the floor.
cells.notes: This is the one max_pulses cell on the table with no datasheet basis at all -- TI TMS 2516 specifies a single 50ms pulse, not a pulse count, so there is nothing in the primary source to cite for a count.

cells.section: 'start programming' (p.138) and AC recommended timing requirements for programming (p.141)
cells.quote: TI TMS 2516, verbatim (p.138): 'a 50-millisecond TTL high-level pulse should be applied to the PGM pin at each address location to be programmed. Maximum pulse width is 55 milliseconds. Locations can be programmed in any order.' No overprogram step appears anywhere in the document -- a single pulse per location is the entire algorithm.
